record.context_brief: Muckenhoupt-weight question for gradients of p-harmonic functions.
record.original_question: Let 1 < p < infinity, let Omega be a connected open subset of R^n with n >= 2, and let u be a nonconstant weak solution of the p-Laplace equation div(|grad u|^(p-2) grad u) = 0 in Omega. Must |grad u| be a Muckenhoupt weight?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.3 (Mukenhoupt). Suppose u solves (1.1) and is not identically constant, is |∇u| a Mukenhoupt weight?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an exponent $1<p<\infty$ and an integer $n\ge 2$. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a connected open set, and let $u\in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ be a non-constant weak solution of the $p$-Laplace equation
$$\operatorname{div} igl(|
abla u|^{p-2}
abla u igr)=0\qquad	ext{in }\Omega,$$
i.e.\ $\int_\Omega |
abla u|^{p-2}
abla u\cdot
abla\varphi\,dx=0$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Recall that a non-negative locally integrable function $w$ on $\Omega$ is a Muckenhoupt $A_q$ weight (for some $1<q<\infty$) if
$$[w]_{A_q}:=\sup_{B}\Bigl( rac{1}{|B|}\int_B w\,dx\Bigr)\Bigl( rac{1}{|B|}\int_B w^{-1/(q-1)}\,dx\Bigr)^{q-1}<\infty,$$
the supremum being taken over all balls $B$ with $\overline{B}\subset\Omega$, and $w\in A_\infty(\Omega)= igcup_{q>1}A_q(\Omega)$.

Question: Must $|
abla u|$ be a Muckenhoupt weight on $\Omega$ (i.e., must $|
abla u|\in A_\infty(\Omega)$, or more strongly belong to some $A_q$ class with $q$ depending only on $n$ and $p$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether $|\nabla u|$ is a Muckenhoupt weight for non-constant weak solutions of the $p$-Laplace equation is posed as an open problem in the literature on $p$-harmonic functions. Web searches return only related results (gradient estimates, $A_\infty$ properties of elliptic measures, $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity by Lewis–DiBenedetto–Tolksdorf), and no published resolution of the general statement was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Definition of $A_p$ weights and their role in harmonic analysis and PDE.
status_evidence.claim: Provides standard background on Muckenhoupt weights underlying the question.

status_evidence.title: On the Lipschitz character of orthotropic p-harmonic functions
status_evidence.claim: Recent works on regularity of $p$-harmonic gradients do not establish the Muckenhoupt property in general.
status_evidence.snippet: Studies regularity of gradients of $p$-harmonic-type functions but not the $A_\infty$ property of $|\nabla u|$.
